ANALYSIS: Interstitial cystitis (IC) is now widely recognized and formally classified by the American Urological Association (AUA) and European Association of Urology (EAU) as **Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome (IC/BPS)** — a chronic pelvic pain condition characterized by bladder pressure, pain, and urinary frequency/urgency in the absence of infection or other identifiable cause. The term “IC/BPS” reflects the spectrum of disease severity and presentation.

The “non-ulcerative subtype” (also called Hunner’s-negative IC/BPS) refers to the more common form (~90% of cases), where cystoscopy under anesthesia shows no glomerulations or Hunner’s ulcers — diagnosis relies on symptom criteria and exclusion of mimics. This contrasts with the less common “ulcerative” (Hunner’s lesion-positive) subtype.

The predicted diagnosis uses current, guideline-aligned terminology and appropriately specifies the most prevalent clinical variant. It is more precise than the reference (“Interstitial cystitis”) without being inconsistent — rather, it refines it using contemporary diagnostic frameworks.
